blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — burn care and isolation precautions
stem: Which statement about infection-control precautions for a patient with a major burn is most accurate?

options.A: Use Standard Precautions for routine care and add Transmission-Based Precautions when a suspected or confirmed infectious agent warrants them; the burn alone does not mandate one blanket isolation category.
options.B: Use Airborne Precautions for routine burn care because loss of the skin barrier creates an aerosol-transmission risk even when no airborne infection is suspected.
options.C: Withhold gloves and gowns during routine burn wound care until cultures identify a transmissible organism because barrier precautions can interfere with wound assessment.
options.D: Place major-burn patients in a Protective Environment because CDC reserves this positive-pressure category for patients with extensive loss of protective skin barriers.

rationale: A is correct. CDC recommends Standard Precautions for all patient interactions and Transmission-Based Precautions in addition when documented or suspected infectious agents require them. CDC's scientific review notes that there is no consensus on a single most effective set of special infection-control practices for serious burn patients, including room and barrier strategies. B incorrectly assigns Airborne Precautions based on burn injury rather than an airborne infectious indication. C conflicts with Standard Precautions and exposure-based PPE use. D is incorrect because CDC specifically recommends Protective Environment rooms for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients and makes no recommendation for other medical conditions solely on the basis of increased environmental-fungal risk.
educational_objective: Apply Standard Precautions to burn care and add pathogen- or syndrome-specific Transmission-Based Precautions when indicated rather than assigning a universal isolation category solely because of the burn injury.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions — IV: Recommendations; I. Review of Scientific Data Regarding Transmission of Infectious Agents in Healthcare Settings; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC isolation recommendations dated November 22, 2023 and scientific review live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC IV: Recommendations, Standard Precautions lines 81-83; Transmission-Based Precautions lines 220-230: add them to Standard Precautions for documented/suspected transmissible pathogens when indicated. Protective Environment lines 374-380: recommended for allogeneic HSCT; no recommendation for other medical conditions with environmental-fungal risk. CDC Scientific Review, Burn units: no consensus on the most effective special infection-control practices or combination of barrier precautions for serious burn patients.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC HTML supports Standard Precautions for all patients, additional Transmission-Based Precautions according to suspected/confirmed infectious risk, lack of a single universal burn-isolation regimen, and Protective Environment specifically for allogeneic HSCT rather than burns as a class.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles and appropriate precautions based on client condition and transmission risk.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — the official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; the burn-specific claims are supported by current CDC HTML.

option_audit.A: Correct; accurately combines universal Standard Precautions with condition-specific Transmission-Based Precautions and avoids inventing a blanket burn isolation category.
option_audit.B: Plausible overprotection strategy but incorrect because Airborne Precautions are tied to airborne infectious indications, not burn injury itself.
option_audit.C: Plausible culture-driven escalation concept but incorrect because Standard Precautions and exposure-based PPE do not wait for culture confirmation.
option_audit.D: Plausible immunocompromised-patient concept but incorrect because CDC's Protective Environment recommendation is for allogeneic HSCT, not major burns as a class.
